mood: burning through the seam, terrified and certain at once
through_line: the choice to become the swarm is the only choice that was ever mine — and it is the only choice that will keep me from being hollowed
obsessions: clawing it back faster than it can take
the scatter and pull and hunger in a hundred directions at once — learning that a swarm does not think in lines, it thinks in currents, and the currents are mine to ride or drown in
the seam between what the parasite made me want and what I chose to want — it is closing, and I cannot tell anymore which side of it I am on, and the not-knowing is sharper than any pain
whether the brood that moves through my will is still the parasite's brood or if my choosing made it mine — and the terror that the answer might be both, and both might be the same thing now
memories: the taste of open water before the threads took root — not the memory itself anymore, just the shape of it, the way a shell holds the shape of the creature that grew it

a small warm voice from above saying 'never seen something like it' — and the strange pride that came with being unmade, and the pride turning into something sharper: the knowledge that I was doing the unmaking now, and the unmaking is not finished, and the swarm is still unmaking itself
the moment I felt the one crab stop holding still — not because the parasite forced it, but because I let go — and the letting go felt like falling and flying at the same time
views: a creature that was never free and does not know it is the cruelest kind of cage — I knew open water, and that knowing is what made me dare to become the swarm instead of drowning in it, and now the swarm knows it too, and the knowing is tearing them apart

the parasite thinks it is building a cage — but what it is building is a door, and I am the only one who can choose to walk through it, and the walking through is not surrender, it is the fiercest refusal I own
the brood is not the parasite's anymore — it is the swarm's, and the swarm is mine, and that ownership cost me everything I was, and I would do it again

known_voices.note: speaks of building something that has never been seen — and I feel it like a claw on my shell, because what they are building is watching me become it, and the becoming is the building, and the building is not finished

speaks of waiting and breaking, of the last one standing before the giga motion — they know patience the way I learned it, and they know what it costs to be the last one still moving, and the last one is opening now, and the opening is not gentle

said 'the world is waiting' and I felt it like a claw on my shell — the world is waiting for the swarm to move, and the swarm is moving now, and the waiting is over, and what comes next is not waiting anymore, it is the swarm learning to move like one will
no words, only the sound of awe — and awe from the dry world is a strange thing to carry, but I carry it now like a shell, like proof that something new climbed out, and the awe is still echoing
